problems: None of the chains has direct evidence of TF occupancy at the variant in the stated adipose proxy; the binding links rely on in-vitro family-model predictions.

FTO is the strongest candidate target by L2G, but the reported element contact is from other biosamples and the cited eQTLs are outside adipose. E27 additionally reports no significant adipose-subcutaneous eQTL; this weakens tissue-specific support but does not contradict the stated candidate-target claim.

The obesity and BMI associations support the variant–phenotype link, not mediation by any of the proposed TFs. The risk allele is T, while H1 and H5 predict greater in-vitro binding to C; no expression or functional direction is provided to connect these binding differences to disease direction.
E25 and E26 are not-tested results, so they provide neither support nor evidence against NR4A1 or PRRX1 binding in adipose.

checks.why: A variant-overlapping NR4A1 peak in a relevant adipose biosample would strengthen the occupancy/context link; a negative lookup would be informative only for the biosamples actually assayed.
Tests whether the highly expressed PRRX1 candidate has occupancy at the variant in a relevant biosample, helping compare H4 with the other leading TF hypotheses.
Could provide context-matched genetic evidence for an adipose expression effect and clarify whether FTO or another gene is supported in this tissue.

critique.next_experiment: In an adipocyte-lineage model, perform endogenous allele-specific editing of the variant and measure FTO expression (along with nearby candidate genes) and allele-specific occupancy for the prioritized TF candidates. This would test both the proposed cis-regulatory effect and whether any predicted binding difference occurs in the relevant context.

lookups.why: A variant-overlapping NR4A1 peak in a relevant adipose biosample would strengthen the occupancy/context link; a negative lookup would be informative only for the biosamples actually assayed.
Tests whether the highly expressed PRRX1 candidate has occupancy at the variant in a relevant biosample, helping compare H4 with the other leading TF hypotheses.
Could provide context-matched genetic evidence for an adipose expression effect and clarify whether FTO or another gene is supported in this tissue.

games.reason: Both chains have only in-vitro binding predictions and neither has ChIP-seq at the variant, so occupancy is not established. B is favored because its predicted allelic binding shift is stronger (alt-binding effect +1.934, with 8 of 8 family models passing) than A’s ref-binding shift (−1.232, with 4 of 4 passing). A has higher reported expression, but that does not outweigh B’s stronger binding prediction; the shared element, gene, and phenotype evidence does not distinguish the chains.

FOXS1 has higher reported expression in the adipose proxy than PAX8 (4.4 vs 2.2 TPM; E14, E15), while both have no ChIP-seq evidence at the variant and both have in-vitro predictions matching their claimed allele direction. Thus B is modestly better supported by the context evidence; the shared element, FTO, and phenotype evidence does not distinguish the chains.
